The platform has two sides. The AI side lets teams build, deploy, and evaluate voice and text agents using a shared knowledge base, embedded evaluations, post-call analysis, data extraction, batch calling, and call transfer. The human side provides a dialer and a live supervision dashboard, from which a person can watch any AI conversation in real time, step in, and hand it back without the customer repeating a word.

Every agent retains memory across channels, so a customer who called yesterday and writes today is recognized and picked up where they left off. The system learns from each human intervention and improves in the direction the team chooses.

Callab AI runs on its own carrier-grade telephony stack and connects natively to Cisco, Mitel, Avaya, SIP trunks, and on-premises PBX systems. Enterprises can adopt it without migrating to the cloud first. The platform maintains SOC 2 controls and serves customers in financial services, healthcare, hospitality, and retail.

Key features:

- AI voice and text agents: Agents handle inbound and outbound conversations across phone, chat, and messaging from a single configuration.

- Live human supervision: Supervisors watch any AI conversation in real time and take over without the customer repeating a word.

- Persistent memory: Every customer's full context is retained across channels and over time.

- AI builder: Teams design, test, and deploy agents without engineering support.

- Embedded evaluations: Every conversation is scored continuously, so performance is measured rather than assumed.

- Self-improving agents: Agents learn from human interventions and get better with every conversation.

- Post-call analysis and data extraction: Every conversation becomes structured, searchable records.

- Batch calling and call transfer: Outbound campaigns run at scale, and conversations move to a human with full context attached.

- Native telephony integration: The platform connects directly to Cisco, Mitel, Avaya, SIP trunks, and on-premises PBX without cloud migration.

- SOC 2 controls: Security and compliance support deployments in regulated industries.

Callab AI delivers every agent production-ready. Our team studies the customer's workflows, internal processes, and existing systems, then builds, tests, and implements the agent on that foundation, so it performs to the organization's own standard from the first live conversation.

Computer vision that makes the industrial workplace, safer Tl;dr: We’re building software that monitors existing cameras in the port, logistics, and manufacturing industries to ensure compliance and identify safety issues.

At Protex AI, we’re on a mission to protect the industrial workforce! We’re building a proactive computer vision tool for workplace safety - empowering industrial Health and Safety (HS) teams to identify risk and danger before it becomes a problem.

🤕 The Problem:
Keeping people safe at work is extremely hard. In the U.S. alone, there were over 5,000 deaths in the workplace in 2019, mainly in the heavy industry space.

Serious workplace injuries cost U.S. businesses circa $62 Billion annually. Until now, safety has been reactive, someone has to get injured, and in some cases fatally before something is done about it.

✅ Problem Solved:
Protex AI’s platform uses privacy-preserving camera monitoring software to provide companies with an always-on guardian angel, protecting their workforce.

The platform plugs into existing CCTV infrastructure and enables HS teams to flexibly translate their document-based safety rules into the real world.

Protex AI takes these rules and autonomously audits the customer’s facility to identify areas of high risk and non-compliance.

HS teams can access this data via a reporting engine and use it in weekly safety meetings, external safety audits, insurance discussions, and legal claims.

The tool integrates seamlessly with existing safety workflows to augment data produced by any manual incident logging system in place.

AI for Corporate Security Cameras Lexius turns existing security cameras into an AI security guard that detects, documents, and alerts incidents like shoplifting and slip-and-falls.

Millions of locations already have cameras but no intelligence. Replacing them costs $50K to $100K per site. Lexius upgrades every camera instantly, no rip and replace, no new hardware.

Real-world camera systems are messy, fragmented, and decades old, and AI breaks on low-quality CCTV. The hard part isn’t the model, it’s making unreliable systems work at scale with accuracy high enough for real decisions.

Lexius starts with security and liability, and becomes the operating system for physical spaces.

AI that turns any camera to an autonomous worker with real-time vision OpenVector transforms any existing camera into an automated 24/7 workforce without requiring new hardware. We've built the world's fastest vision-language model inference engine that allows users to simply describe a task in plain English and automatically build a custom AI vision model to monitor their feed. When it detects an important physical event—like a stalled production cycle, a safety violation, or a waiting customer—it operates a computer just like a human to take immediate action. It integrates with legacy systems, makes calls, sends emails, updates a POS/CRM, or triggers webhooks in real time. OpenVector enables any camera to do real work.

AI cameras for workforce monitoring Optifye deploys AI cameras in factories to monitor operator productivity & SOP adherence in real-time.

We work with 5 out of the 10 largest autocomponent manufacturers in India!

Building the next generation of AI enabled monitoring Security cameras don’t stop crime. They film it. Traditional monitoring does one job: watching an empty site after hours. It misses anything more complex, and anything that happens during the day. When something does happen, it sends an alert and leaves the response to you.

Synara is the AI monitoring station for the cameras that are already installed. It needs no new hardware and watches day and night. It understands far more than intruders: falls, guns, fights. And it owns the response. Synara verifies incidents in seconds, talks intruders down on site or sends police a verified alarm, then coordinates with officers on who’s on site and where people are safe, until the insurance claim is resolved.

Because AI does the watching, monitoring becomes drastically cheaper and more accurate. Synara sells through security integrators under their own brand, so every camera they’ve installed becomes recurring revenue.

Our customers are the $100M+ contractors building America’s data centers.

The AGI race is a construction race. More than 40% of America’s 2026 data centers are late, and every month of delay is a gift to the CCP. They’re late because contractors still coordinate every jobsite by phone and spreadsheet.

Contractors sell their work at fixed prices, so every hour a crew waits comes out of their margin. One broken machine stops every crew behind it, and the repair invoice shows only a fraction of the cost. The rest lands in idle crews and higher bids on the next job.

Adam, our AI operator, runs equipment operations for the whole company’s profit. He prices every idle hour, picks the repair with the lowest total cost, audits every bill before it’s paid, reallocates idle machines to the jobs that need them, and tells the company which machines to buy, repair, or sell. Managers approve every cost and Adam handles the coordination in between.

In three months, Adam increased operating profit by $4.21M a year for a $500M electrical contracting customer: a 12% increase. Across customers, the time people spend coordinating each repair fell 93%, and equipment downtime fell 30%.

We crossed $2M ARR three months after our first invoice, with five enterprise customers and a five-person team. Customers pay annually upfront, so we’re cash-flow positive. Carma sells no parts, rentals, or machines, so Adam’s only incentive is our customer’s profit.
